caption:
An AI just moved onto your website's design canvas and started working like a real designer.

Framer has quietly been "the no-code builder that looks like Figma" for years. But its July 2026 update, announced by co-founder Jurre Houtkamp and featured on Product Hunt's weekly leaderboard, changes what it actually is.

You can now drop an AI agent directly onto the canvas and have it design sections, write copy, analyze your existing site, and organize your pages — in the same visual editor a human would use. And it's not locked to one AI: you can connect Claude Code or Codex and let those work the canvas instead. Product Hunt's own AI Agents roundup singled it out for turning prompts into sites that actually look finished.

The part that might matter more for anyone with a portfolio, a passion project, or a site they're scared to touch: Branching. You fork your live site, mess with a full redesign in the fork, and only merge it back if you like it. Nothing you try can break what's already live.

There's also a new Community space where people are sharing (and getting paid for) templates and components they built — so a weekend project can quietly become income.

The honest catch: if you already use Framer daily, this won't feel brand new. And the AI pass is still early — complex, highly custom designs will likely need a human cleanup afterward.

Send this to whoever keeps saying "I've been meaning to redo my site" for a year. Save it so you have it when you're ready to actually try. Full breakdown — link in bio.
